config.title: print styles (@media print)

intro.title: print styles (@media print)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage and learn how to make it look great when printed. You will use CSS print styles with the @media print rule to control what appears on paper, such as hiding unnecessary elements and adjusting colors. The main technology you'll work with is CSS, specifically media queries for print. This is a beginner-friendly way to ensure your web content is printer-friendly and professional.
intro.usecase: Print styles are essential for creating user-friendly, printer-friendly versions of web pages. In real software, developers use @media print to ensure that dashboards, invoices, and reports print cleanly by hiding interactive elements like navigation menus, buttons, and ads, while preserving key data and layout. For example, an e-commerce order confirmation page might hide the header, footer, and promotional banners when printed, leaving only the order details and shipping information. This pattern is also applied to printable forms, documentation pages, and financial statements to save ink and improve readability on paper.

objectives: Implement a print media query to target print-specific styling
Configure CSS rules to hide non-essential elements when printing
Apply print-optimized typography and spacing for better readability

Initialize print-specific page breaks to control content flow
Integrate print stylesheets with existing screen styles

steps.title: Add basic screen styles to the content
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules inside a <style> element in the <head> to style the HTML elements for normal screen viewing. Style the body with a light background, the header with a dark background and white text, and paragraphs with a readable font size and line height.
steps.hint: Place a <style> tag in the <head> section and write CSS rules for body, header, and p elements.

steps.title: Introduce the @media print rule
steps.instruction: Inside the existing <style> element, add an @media print rule that will contain all print-specific styles.
steps.hint: Use the syntax @media print { /* your print styles will go here */ }

steps.title: Test print styles using browser print preview
steps.instruction: Open your browser's print preview to see how the print styles affect the page appearance.
steps.hint: In most browsers, you can access print preview via File → Print or by pressing Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on Mac). Look for the 'Print Preview' option to see how the page would look when printed.
